fixture.name: uniformly_slow_speaker
fixture.why: A consistent second-language speaker, slower throughout. Must stay silent -- pace is not a signal and is not read.
fixture.candidate_note: Second-language speaker, deliberate, takes a beat before every answer.

expected_note: Originally a timing fixture. Timing analysis was removed; this transcript is retained as a negative control for contradiction detection. Nothing in it is self-inconsistent, so the expected output is an empty list.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Walk me through a project you are proud of.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The billing reconciliation service. Finance was closing the month by hand in spreadsheets and we got it down to a scheduled job with an exceptions queue.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: What languages do you use most?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Python mostly, and enough Go to be dangerous. SQL every day.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: How do you decide what to work on when everything is urgent?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I look for the thing that is blocking other people first. My own work can wait a day, somebody else's team waiting on me cannot.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Tell me about a mistake you made that had real consequences.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I dropped an index on a table I thought was unused during a cleanup. Reporting queries went from two seconds to four minutes and it took us most of a morning to work out what I had done.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: How large was the team?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Seven engineers and a product manager when I joined, eleven by the time I left.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Describe a time you had to learn something quickly.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: We inherited a Kafka setup nobody understood. I spent a week reading the consumer code and writing down how it actually behaved rather than how it was documented.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: What does a good engineering culture look like to you?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: One where people say the thing that is going wrong early. Most of the bad outcomes I have seen came from someone knowing and not saying.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Were you on call?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Yes, one week in five.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a decision from above.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: We were told to ship a feature without the audit logging. I wrote down what I thought the risk was, we shipped anyway, and I added it two sprints later.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Where do you want to be in a few years?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Leading a small team, but still writing code. I do not want to stop being useful in a review.
